notes: ACTIVE relation pack (upgraded from pilot). No invented Sn/Sp. Traditional MTrP maps labeled traditional. No Travell verbatim.

relations.source_structure: possible secondary headache (vascular, infection, mass, trauma)
relations.clinical_context: Thunderclap, worst headache, focal neurology, fever/stiff neck, trauma with vomiting/confusion, or other SNOOP-type features.
supporting_evidence: Secondary-headache red-flag frameworks exist to trigger medical/emergency pathways
MSK or myofascial hypotheses are inappropriate first steps

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Safety screen, not a physiotherapy test accuracy claim.

limitations: SNOOP is a mnemonic, not a validated single score
Absence of red flags does not prove primary headache
recommended_examination: Urgent medical pathway per local protocol

references.citation: Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain: Revision 2017 (CPG). JOSPT — associated cervical red flags.
ICHD-3: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition — secondary vs primary framing (qualitative).

relations.source_structure: upper cervical somatic structures (clinical cervicogenic headache construct)
relations.clinical_context: Headache provoked or eased by neck movement/posture, with upper-cervical findings, after SNOOP screen.
supporting_evidence: Neck Pain CPGs include cervicogenic contribution as a clinical pattern
Evidence reviews emphasize overlap with primary headache and lack of a single confirmatory test

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: No isolated MSK test confirms cervicogenic headache. Do not invent Sn/Sp.

limitations: Migraine and cervicogenic features often coexist
Spurling does not diagnose headache source
recommended_examination: C0–C2 AROM and familiar-pain reproduction with cervical tests
Do not treat migraine features as trigger points

references.citation: Bogduk N, Govind J. Cervicogenic headache: an assessment of the evidence on diagnosis, management, and treatment. Lancet Neurol. 2009.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain: Revision 2017 (CPG). JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: Pulsatile headache with nausea/photophobia ± aura, or bilateral pressing tension-type pattern, with or without neck pain.
supporting_evidence: ICHD-3 classifies primary headache by pattern, not by a physical test
Neck pain does not exclude migraine

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Pattern recognition, not Sn/Sp of palpation.

limitations: Neck pain is common in migraine
Do not relabel migraine as MTrP
recommended_examination: Cervical exam as adjunct, not replacement

references.citation: Headache Classification Committee of the IHS. The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition. Cephalalgia. 2018.

relations.clinical_context: Palpation reproduces familiar head pain after SNOOP and after primary vs cervicogenic framing.
supporting_evidence: Classical maps describe head referral from cervical/shoulder girdle muscles (traditional class only)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: MTrP palpation reliability limited (Lucas 2009). Found ≠ cause.

limitations: Traditional maps are not absolute anatomy
Must not replace SNOOP or migraine reasoning
Do not attribute vertigo solely to SCM
recommended_examination: Familiar pain on palpation plus cervical AROM

references.citation: Tough EA et al. Variability of criteria used to diagnose myofascial trigger point pain syndrome. 2007.
Lucas N et al. Reliability of physical examination for diagnosis of myofascial trigger points. Clin J Pain. 2009.

relations.clinical_context: Headache or temporal pain with jaw load, clicking, or preauricular tenderness after SNOOP.
supporting_evidence: TMD and primary headache frequently overlap clinically
Jaw findings do not exclude migraine or cervicogenic contribution

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Pattern coexistence — no invented Sn/Sp for jaw palpation.

limitations: Must not skip SNOOP
Dental/occlusion leaps unsupported
recommended_examination: Jaw opening/load familiar pain as adjunct

references.citation: ICHD-3 — secondary vs primary headache framing including TMD-related.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG — associated headache framing.

relations.source_structure: upper cervical / cervicogenic headache clinical construct
relations.clinical_context: Suspected cervicogenic pattern; flexion-rotation or upper-cervical tests negative or poorly tolerated.
supporting_evidence: No isolated MSK test confirms or excludes cervicogenic headache
Overlap with migraine/TTH is substantial

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp for flexion-rotation as absolute exclusion.

limitations: Irritability limits testing
Positive test also non-specific

references.citation: Bogduk N, Govind J. Cervicogenic headache evidence assessment. Lancet Neurol.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: After SNOOP: unilateral headache associated with neck movement/posture and familiar pain on cervical testing.
supporting_evidence: Neck Pain CPGs include cervicogenic contribution as a clinical pattern
Pattern + familiar reproduction > single special test

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Qualitative pattern only; no invented cluster Sn/Sp.

limitations: Migraine overlap
Spurling does not diagnose headache source
recommended_examination: Do not treat migraine features as trigger points

references.citation: Bogduk N, Govind J. Cervicogenic headache. Lancet Neurol.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: Migraine pattern with neck pain — neck pain does not exclude migraine and does not prove cervicogenic alone.
supporting_evidence: Neck pain is common in migraine
ICHD-3 classifies by pattern, not by a physical test

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Coexistence framing — not Sn/Sp of palpation.

limitations: Do not relabel migraine as MTrP
SNOOP still required when atypical
recommended_examination: Cervical exam as adjunct, not replacement

references.citation: Headache Classification Committee of the IHS. ICHD-3. Cephalalgia.
Bogduk N, Govind J. Cervicogenic headache — overlap framing.

relations.source_structure: mild traumatic brain injury / concussion pathways
relations.clinical_context: Head trauma with worsening headache, vomiting, confusion, focal neurology, or anticoagulation — urgent pathway.
supporting_evidence: Post-traumatic red-flag frameworks trigger medical/emergency evaluation

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Safety pathway, not an MSK test.

limitations: Not all post-trauma headache is emergency
Local concussion protocols prevail
recommended_examination: Stop elective MSK cascade if red flags
Urgent medical pathway per local protocol

references.citation: ICHD-3 — post-traumatic headache / secondary framing (qualitative).
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG — trauma red-flag framing.

relations.source_structure: giant cell arteritis / temporal arteritis construct
relations.clinical_context: Older adult with new temporal headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, or visual change — urgent medical pathway.
supporting_evidence: GCA is a sight-threatening emergency differential for new temporal headache in older adults

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Safety pathway — do not invent Sn/Sp for temporal palpation.

limitations: Not all temporal pain in older adults is GCA
Do not delay referral
recommended_examination: Do not treat as cervicogenic or MTrP
red_flags: Age typically ≥50 with new temporal headache

references.citation: ICHD-3 — headache attributed to GCA framing (qualitative).
GCA clinical red-flag pathway literature — urgent steroids/medical care.

relations.clinical_context: Occipital headache with familiar suboccipital palpation after SNOOP and primary vs cervicogenic framing — traditional only.
supporting_evidence: Classical maps describe occipital/orbital patterns (traditional class only)
limitations: Must not replace SNOOP or migraine reasoning
Traditional ≠ absolute anatomy

references.citation: Tough EA et al. 2007; Lucas N et al. 2009 — MTrP caution.
Bogduk N, Govind J. Cervicogenic headache — avoid muscle-map certainty.

relations.target_region: dizziness / imbalance with or without headache
relations.clinical_context: True spinning vertigo, HINTS/central clues, or vascular features — not attributed to SCM trigger points.
supporting_evidence: Vestibular and vascular dizziness require medical/vestibular pathways
Do not attribute vertigo solely to SCM (traditional maps)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Safety/pattern differentiation — no invented Sn/Sp for SCM.

limitations: Cervicogenic dizziness construct is controversial
Central causes first if red flags
recommended_examination: Do not treat vertigo as MTrP
red_flags: Sudden severe dizziness with neuro deficit

references.citation: ICHD-3 — vestibular migraine / secondary dizziness framing (qualitative).
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG — red flags; avoid SCM-vertigo leaps.
